chunks: Do you not realize? I am not giving you any news, but I am recounting by the bounty of Allah,

that a number of people from among the muhajirun and the ansar fell as martyrs in the way of Allah the Exalted, and each of them has a distinction, until when one of our martyrs was killed, he was called the Chief of the Martyrs, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) singled him out with seventy takbirs during his funeral prayer!
ai.seo_question: What unique honor did the Prophet bestow upon a specific martyr from the Muhajirun and Ansar?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses this passage to assert the superior merit of the Ahl al-Bayt and early companions over the Umayyads, specifically highlighting the unique honor of the 'Chief of the Martyrs' (often identified as Hamzah or a specific companion in this context) who received seventy takbirs in his funeral prayer. This detail underscores the distinct spiritual rank of the martyrs in Shia tradition, where the number of takbirs signifies the magnitude of their sacrifice and divine favor. The reference serves as a rhetorical counter to Muawiya’s claims of legitimacy by emphasizing merit (fadilah) over political power.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Do you not realize it? I am not giving you any news: I am just recounting Allāh’s bounty,

namely that a number of people from among the muhājirūn (immigrants from Mecca) and anṣār (helpers) fell as martyrs in the way of Allāh the Sublime, and that each of them is distinguished (on that account), but when one of us secured martyrdom he was named the Chief of all martyrs, and the Messenger of Allāh (S) gave him the peculiar honour of saying seventy takbīr (Allāhu akbar) during his funeral prayer.
